sentences.zh: 而有时这会次于对你所在党派的支持。

sentences.en: It's an unfortunate thing because, in the long run, it's very costly.
sentences.zh: 这是一件不幸的事，因为从长远来看，代价非常高昂。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: I'm talking with Alan Alda before a live audience in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 我正在华盛顿特区与艾伦·阿尔达进行现场观众访谈。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'm going to ask Alan about some techniques that actors learn
sentences.zh: 回来后，我将向艾伦请教一些演员学习的技巧，

sentences.en: that can help us all become better communicators.
sentences.zh: 这些技巧可以帮助我们大家都成为更好的沟通者。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收看。

sentences.en: I want to talk about another situation involving a doctor.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈另一个涉及医生的情境。

sentences.en: This one involved a doctor, I believe, in Chile, where you needed medical attention.
sentences.zh: 我相信这次是在智利，当时你需要医疗救助。

sentences.en: And this doctor treated you very differently than the dentist treated you in the other situation.
sentences.zh: 那位医生对待你的方式，与之前那个情境中牙医对待你的方式截然不同。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It was the best example of communication I had ever heard.
sentences.zh: 那是我听过的最好的沟通案例。

sentences.en: My problem was that I had an intestine that had twisted, got caught in something, and had choked off the blood supply.
sentences.zh: 我的问题是肠道扭转，被什么东西卡住了，导致血液供应中断。

sentences.en: And about a yard of my intestine was dying.
sentences.zh: 大约有一码长的肠子正在坏死。

sentences.en: And in the middle of the night, I was taken to a hospital, and he recognized almost immediately what was wrong with me.
sentences.zh: 半夜里，我被送进医院，他几乎立刻就认出了我的问题所在。

sentences.en: And he didn't use fancy language.
sentences.zh: 他没有使用花哨的术语。

sentences.en: He explained to me in the simplest, most, the plainest language.
sentences.zh: 他用最简单、最平实的语言向我解释。

sentences.en: Here's what's happened, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，情况是这样的。

sentences.en: Some of your intestine has gone bad.
sentences.zh: 你的一部分肠子坏了。

sentences.en: And we have to cut out the bad part and sew the two good ends together.
sentences.zh: 我们必须切除坏掉的部分，把两端好的缝合在一起。

sentences.en: You can't get simpler than that.
sentences.zh: 再简单不过了。

sentences.en: And that was absolutely accurate.
sentences.zh: 而且那绝对准确。

sentences.en: There wasn't anything about that, as clear as it was, that wasn't true.
sentences.zh: 尽管说得很清楚，但其中没有任何不实之处。

sentences.en: And by the way, he wasn't just speaking clearly.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他不仅仅是说话清晰。

sentences.en: I remember so vividly his leaning down, looking into my eyes, watching my face to see if I understood him.
sentences.zh: 我清楚地记得他俯下身，直视我的眼睛，观察我的表情，看我是否听懂了。

sentences.en: That was the essence of good communication.
sentences.zh: 这就是良好沟通的精髓。

sentences.en: He was watching me to see if I was getting it.
sentences.zh: 他在观察我，看我是否理解了。

sentences.en: Did I understand him or did I have that funny look on my face?
sentences.zh: 我是听懂了，还是脸上露出了困惑的表情？

sentences.en: And the answer to your original notion is things I've learned as an actor have made me understand the importance of how that doctor, Nelson Zepeda, in Chile,
sentences.zh: 对于你最初提到的观点，答案是：我作为演员学到的东西让我明白了那位医生——智利的尼尔森·泽佩达——的重要性，

sentences.en: in the middle of the night, 13 or 14 years ago, how he made a real effort to communicate with me.
sentences.zh: 13或14年前的那个深夜，他是如何真正努力与我沟通的。

sentences.en: And it made all the difference for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说意义重大。

sentences.en: I understand the technical term for this procedure is an end-to-end anastomosis, if I'm saying that correctly.
sentences.zh: 我明白这个手术的专业术语是“端对端吻合术”，如果我没说错的话。

sentences.en: And I can just imagine the doctor had said, I'm going to perform an end-to-end anastomosis, Mr. Alda, how that would have made you feel.
sentences.zh: 我简直可以想象，如果医生说“阿尔达先生，我要为你进行端对端吻合术”，你会是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Well, I would have felt the way I did with the dentiSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我会感觉和面对那位牙医时一样。

sentences.en: I want to ask you about another thing you mentioned in the book.
sentences.zh: 我想问你书中提到的另一件事。

sentences.en: You cite Don Hewitt, who was the creator of the television show 60 Minutes,
sentences.zh: 你提到了唐·休伊特，他是电视节目《60分钟》的创作者，

sentences.en: and you say that Don had a simple four-word question he would ask when people pitch stories for the show that in some ways was the essence of the success of the show.
sentences.zh: 你说唐在人们为节目推销故事时，会问一个简单的四个字的问题，这在某种程度上是该节目成功的精髓。

sentences.en: Yes, he loved that story, and I know he loved it because I knew Don for about 30 years, and he told me that story three times a year.
sentences.zh: 是的，他很喜欢那个故事，我知道他喜欢，因为我认识唐大约30年了，他一年会跟我讲三次那个故事。

sentences.en: And the story was that when somebody would come into his office, a producer, and say, I've got a great idea for a segment on the show,
sentences.zh: 故事是这样的：当有人——比如制片人——走进他的办公室说“我有个关于节目片段的好点子”时，

sentences.en: they'd start to tell about some infraction of the banking regulations or something like that.
sentences.zh: 他们会开始讲述一些违反银行法规之类的事情。

sentences.en: And he'd hold up his hand and say, wait a minute, four words, tell me a story.
sentences.zh: 他会举起手说：“等一下，四个字：讲个故事。”

sentences.en: And he felt that that was what made the show so successful all those years.
sentences.zh: 他觉得这就是该节目多年来如此成功的原因。

sentences.en: It was number one for a couple of decades at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 它至少有二十年稳居第一。

sentences.en: And I think he was right about it being part of the success of the show.
sentences.zh: 我认为他说得对，这确实是节目成功的一部分。

sentences.en: And I think it's because we all tell stories to one another.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这是因为我们都在互相讲故事。

sentences.en: We listen better to a story.
sentences.zh: 我们听故事时会更专注。

sentences.en: We get involved when we hear a story.
sentences.zh: 听到故事时，我们会投入其中。

sentences.en: And his stories would always have a middle part where the fortunes shifted and you thought to yourself, this isn't what I thought this was going to be about.
sentences.zh: 他的故事总会有一个中间部分，情节发生转折，你会想：这跟我预想的不一样。

sentences.en: This is a deeper question or this look at the turn this took.
sentences.zh: 这是一个更深层的问题，或者看看这个转折。

sentences.en: Now this is affecting me in a different way.
sentences.zh: 现在这对我产生了不同的影响。

sentences.en: The importance of the middle, I think, is so huge.
sentences.zh: 我认为中间部分的重要性非常巨大。

sentences.en: You know, I was interviewing a researcher at Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当时正在采访哥伦比亚大学的一位研究员。

sentences.en: Her name is Xiaodong Lin, and she's done a lot of work looking at trying to get children interested in science.
sentences.zh: 她叫林晓东，她做了大量工作，试图让孩子们对科学产生兴趣。

sentences.en: And she finds something really fascinating that speaks to exactly what you just talked about,
sentences.zh: 她发现了一些非常迷人的东西，正好印证了你刚才所说的，

sentences.en: which is the traditional way we have of teaching science is to tell people, you know, there was this great physicist, Albert Einstein,
sentences.zh: 那就是我们传统的科学教学方式是告诉人们：有一位伟大的物理学家，阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦，

sentences.en: and he was the greatest genius the world has ever known.
sentences.zh: 他是世界上有史以来最伟大的天才。

sentences.en: And he came up with theories that even today many people struggle to understand.
sentences.zh: 他提出的理论即使在今天，许多人也难以理解。

sentences.en: So that's the classic way we tell science stories.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们讲述科学故事的经典方式。

sentences.en: And what she found was that instead of doing that, if you tell a story which says something along the lines of,
sentences.zh: 而她发现，如果不这样做，而是讲一个类似这样的故事：

sentences.en: you know, there was a time when Einstein was working on a problem and he got so stuck that he couldn't figure out the math.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一次爱因斯坦在研究一个问题时，卡住了，算不出数学题。

sentences.en: And he needed help to figure out the math.
sentences.zh: 他需要帮助来算出数学题。

sentences.en: And he reached out to somebody else saying, I can't figure out the math to this.
sentences.zh: 于是他向别人求助说：我算不出这个数学题。

sentences.en: Can you please help me?
sentences.zh: 你能帮帮我吗？

sentences.en: When you tell stories that involve struggle and obstacles and failures about scientists,
sentences.zh: 当你讲述涉及科学家奋斗、障碍和失败的故事时，

sentences.en: not only does this hold people's attention, but kids are now able to say, I can see myself being a scientist because I need help with math.
sentences.zh: 这不仅能吸引人们的注意力，孩子们现在也能说：我能想象自己成为一名科学家，因为我在数学上需要帮助。

sentences.en: I turn to somebody else to get help for math.
sentences.zh: 我会向别人求助来解决数学问题。

sentences.en: And this idea that the obstacle in some ways is what makes the story the story is, I think, what you mean by the middle.
sentences.zh: 这种认为障碍在某种程度上成就了故事的观点，我想就是你所说的“中间部分”。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And underneath all of that is trying to be aware of what the listener is going through while you tell them about this.
sentences.zh: 而这一切的基础是，在你讲述时，要意识到听众正在经历什么。

sentences.en: Because you might have the best message in the world.
sentences.zh: 因为你可能拥有世界上最好的信息。

sentences.en: And a lot of people think good communication is devising a really good message that's logical, clear, you know, clear to you anyway.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为良好的沟通就是设计出一条逻辑清晰、表达明确的信息——至少对你自己来说是清晰的。

sentences.en: The question is, how clear is it and how interesting is it to the person you're trying to tell it to or the layer of the public you're trying to tell it to.
sentences.zh: 问题是，对于你试图讲述的对象，或者你试图触达的公众层面来说，它有多清晰、多有趣。

sentences.en: If you can imagine what they're going through while they hear your story,
sentences.zh: 如果你能想象他们在听你的故事时正在经历什么，

sentences.en: then you're relating to them in the same way that I found I related to the other actor when I was on the stage.
sentences.zh: 那么你与他们的联系方式，就和我发现自己在舞台上与另一位演员建立联系的方式一样。

sentences.en: One of the really interesting things you did was you have brought in groups of engineering students and other technical people and you have taught them improv.
sentences.zh: 你做过一件非常有趣的事情，就是你引入了工程系学生和其他技术人员，并教他们即兴表演。

sentences.en: You've taught them, you've put them through three hours of improv games.
sentences.zh: 你教过他们，让他们进行了三个小时的即兴游戏。

sentences.en: Why in the world would you do that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要那样做？

sentences.en: Because when I left the science show, I realized that the reason that the show worked was because we had a real connection between us.
sentences.zh: 因为当我离开那个科学节目时，我意识到节目之所以成功，是因为我们之间有真正的联系。

sentences.en: It wasn't an ordinary interview.
sentences.zh: 那不是普通的采访。

sentences.en: I never went in with a set of questions, not after the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有带着一套问题去采访，至少在开始之后没有。

sentences.en: I went in just being curious and really good and ignorant.
sentences.zh: 我只是带着好奇心，表现得很好，而且一无所知。

sentences.en: It's good to be ignorant as long as you're curious.
sentences.zh: 只要你保持好奇心，无知是一件好事。

sentences.en: Not so good if you're not curious.
sentences.zh: 如果你不好奇，那就没那么好了。

sentences.en: So I would be willing to reveal my ignorance to them so they knew where I was in my understanding of their work.
sentences.zh: 所以我愿意向他们展示我的无知，这样他们就知道我对他们工作的理解处于什么水平。

sentences.en: And then if I didn't understand what they were saying, I'd grab them by the lapels and shake them.
sentences.zh: 然后，如果我不明白他们在说什么，我会抓住他们的衣领摇晃他们。

sentences.en: Tell me again.
sentences.zh: 再讲一遍。

sentences.en: So they forgot about the camera.
sentences.zh: 于是他们忘记了摄像机。

sentences.en: They forgot about the lectures they had given on this.
sentences.zh: 他们忘记了自己曾就此发表过的演讲。

sentences.en: They were just trying to make me understand it.
sentences.zh: 他们只是试图让我听懂。

sentences.en: And I realized that what I was doing was relating to them and they were relating to me in the same way two actors do, where they let each other in to their field of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我所做的是与他们建立联系，他们也以两位演员之间的方式与我建立联系，他们让对方进入自己的意识领域。

sentences.en: So I thought the best way to train people to do that is through improvisation training.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为训练人们做到这一点的最好方法是通过即兴表演训练。

sentences.en: And I tried it out with a group of engineers.
sentences.zh: 我在一组工程师身上试了一下。

sentences.en: And after three hours, they were so much better talking about their work.
sentences.zh: 三个小时后，他们在谈论自己的工作时表现得好多了。

sentences.en: I thought, I think we got something here.
sentences.zh: 我想，我觉得我们找到门道了。

sentences.en: We can make this work as the basis of training.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把它作为培训的基础。

sentences.en: And soon after that, we started what's now known as the Alan Aldis Center for Communicating Science at Stony Brook University in New York.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，我们创办了现在位于纽约州石溪大学的艾伦·阿尔达科学传播中心。

sentences.en: And we've taught, in the past eight years, we've taught almost 10,000 scientists and doctors to communicate better,
sentences.zh: 在过去的八年里，我们已经培训了近一万名科学家和医生，让他们更好地进行沟通，

sentences.en: starting with classes in improvisation and then moving on to working out the content of what they're going to say.
sentences.zh: 从即兴表演课程开始，然后转向打磨他们要表达的内容。

sentences.en: The thing is, if you really relate to the other person, that has an effect on the content of what you're going to say to them.
sentences.zh: 关键是，如果你真的与对方建立了联系，这会影响你对他们所说内容的效果。

sentences.en: You're not going to use certain words.
sentences.zh: 你不会使用某些词汇。

sentences.en: You're not going to use certain concepts.
sentences.zh: 你不会使用某些概念。

sentences.en: You're going to make sure they're with you along the way.
sentences.zh: 你会确保他们一路跟得上你的思路。

sentences.en: You have a wonderful story in your book about a moment you were trying to catch a cab.
sentences.zh: 你的书中有一个精彩的故事，讲的是你试图打车的那一刻。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I didn't know about you is, apparently, in your 20s, among the many, many things you've done in your life,
sentences.zh: 我不知道关于你的一件事是，显然，在你20多岁时，在你一生中做过的许多许多事情中，

sentences.en: you were apparently a cab driver for a brief period of your life.
sentences.zh: 你曾短暂地做过一段时间出租车司机。

sentences.en: And in the story, you were trying to catch a cab.
sentences.zh: 在故事里，你当时正试图打车。

sentences.en: And the driver of the taxi basically asks you where you want to go before he lets you into the cab.
sentences.zh: 出租车司机在让你上车前，基本上先问你要去哪里。

sentences.en: Right, because in New York, at around 3.30 or 4 in the afternoon, the cabs are heading home.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为在纽约，下午3点半或4点左右，出租车都要回家了。

sentences.en: Their shift is over.
sentences.zh: 他们的班次结束了。

sentences.en: And they don't want to take you unless you're going somewhere near where their garage is.
sentences.zh: 除非你要去的地方靠近他们的车库，否则他们不想载你。

sentences.en: So I did drive a cab.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实开过出租车。

sentences.en: And I know that the law is if somebody wants to get in the cab, you have to let them in whether you want to take them or not.
sentences.zh: 我知道法律规定，如果有人想上车，无论你想不想载他们，你都必须让他们上车。

sentences.en: So I don't like these conversations about where you're going, because I know they're not supposed to ask.
sentences.zh: 所以我讨厌这些关于你要去哪里的对话，因为我知道他们不应该问。

sentences.en: They're supposed to take you.
sentences.zh: 他们应该载你。

sentences.en: Now, I had been doing all this work when this cab pulled over.
sentences.zh: 当时我一直在做这些工作，这时一辆出租车停了下来。

sentences.en: And what the improvising work does is it actually builds up your empathy.
sentences.zh: 即兴表演工作的作用是它实际上增强了你的同理心。

sentences.en: You get very good at being able to figure out what the other person is going through emotionally.
sentences.zh: 你变得非常擅长弄清楚对方在情感上经历了什么。

sentences.en: So now this cab driver pulls over.
sentences.zh: 所以现在这个出租车司机停了下来。

sentences.en: He says, where are you going?
sentences.zh: 他问，你要去哪儿？

sentences.en: And I start to get crazy mad.
sentences.zh: 我开始变得极其愤怒。

sentences.en: Where am I going?
sentences.zh: 我要去哪儿？

sentences.en: You've got to take me no matter where I'm going.
sentences.zh: 无论我要去哪儿，你都得载我。

sentences.en: But instead of that, I think, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 但转念一想，等一下。

sentences.en: It's the time of day when he's switching shifts.
sentences.zh: 现在正是他换班的时间。

sentences.en: He's got to give the cab to somebody else.
sentences.zh: 他得把车交给别人。

sentences.en: I understand why he's saying it.
sentences.zh: 我理解他为什么这么说。

sentences.en: And it helped me accept it.
sentences.zh: 这帮我接受了现实。

sentences.en: So I told him where I was going, gave him the address.
sentences.zh: 所以我告诉了他我要去的地方，给了他地址。

sentences.en: He said, get in.
sentences.zh: 他说，上车吧。

sentences.en: So I thought, OK.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧。

sentences.en: So that felt pretty good.
sentences.zh: 感觉还不错。

sentences.en: Then he says, what's the cross street?
sentences.zh: 然后他说，交叉路口在哪？

sentences.en: And I started to get crazy angry again.
sentences.zh: 我又开始变得极其愤怒。

sentences.en: He's supposed to know the cross street.
sentences.zh: 他应该知道交叉路口。

sentences.en: But now I'm all empathized up, you know.
sentences.zh: 但现在我充满了同理心，你知道的。

sentences.en: So I said to him, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 所以我对他说，等一下。

sentences.en: I'm looking it up on my iPhone.
sentences.zh: 我正在用iPhone查。

sentences.en: I'm helping him out.
sentences.zh: 我在帮他。

sentences.en: He said, you know, you're a nice person.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道吗，你是个好人。

sentences.en: People get in this cab.
sentences.zh: 人们坐上这辆车。

sentences.en: They don't care about me at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不在乎我。

sentences.en: I'm really impressed with this.
sentences.zh: 我真的对此印象深刻。

sentences.en: I said, well, thanks.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，谢谢。

sentences.en: He said, I've been trying to go to the bathroom for the last half hour.
sentences.zh: 他说，我已经在过去半小时里一直想去洗手间了。

sentences.en: I said, well, then just drop me off.
sentences.zh: 我说，那你就把我放下吧。

sentences.en: Don't take me to the corner.
sentences.zh: 别把我送到街角。

sentences.en: Don't go all the way around the block.
sentences.zh: 别绕着街区转圈。

sentences.en: He said, no, I'm taking you right where you're going.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，我要把你送到你要去的地方。

sentences.en: You're a nice person.
sentences.zh: 你是个好人。

sentences.en: The guy, he's giving up his kidneys for me.
sentences.zh: 那个人，他为了我连肾都愿意捐出来。

sentences.en: So the funny thing was, the exercises that we do in improv give you a little more empathy.
sentences.zh: 所以有趣的是，我们在即兴表演中做的练习能让你多一点同理心。

sentences.en: And here was an example that I was using it in real life.
sentences.zh: 而这就是我在现实生活中运用它的一个例子。

sentences.en: And it was helping in the communication I had with this guy.
sentences.zh: 它确实改善了我与那个人的沟通。

sentences.en: I got where I wanted to go.
sentences.zh: 我到达了我想去的地方。

sentences.en: I felt so much better about it.
sentences.zh: 我对此感觉好多了。

sentences.en: And I've noticed that the more empathy I have, the less annoying other people are.
sentences.zh: 而且我注意到，我的同理心越强，别人就越不会让我感到烦躁。

sentences.en: You came up with a very interesting exercise at one point where you were trying to increase
sentences.zh: 你曾经想出了一个非常有趣的练习，当时你试图增加

sentences.en: and train your own ability to empathize with others.
sentences.zh: 并训练自己与他人产生共情的能力。

sentences.en: And you came up with a system to actually sit down with friends or colleagues.
sentences.zh: 你还想出了一套系统，可以真正坐下来与朋友或同事进行练习。

sentences.en: What did you do?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么做的？

sentences.en: Well, I realized I couldn't constantly be going to improv exercises.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我意识到我不可能一直去做即兴表演练习。

sentences.en: And I noticed that my empathy would sort of wane after a while.
sentences.zh: 而且我注意到，过了一段时间，我的同理心会逐渐减弱。

sentences.en: You know, we live stressful lives.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们的生活压力很大。

sentences.en: And one scientist told me that she felt that stress, you know, the stress hormones in your body,
sentences.zh: 一位科学家告诉我，她觉得压力，你知道，身体里的压力荷尔蒙，

sentences.en: when they build up, they kind of damp your empathy to some extent.
sentences.zh: 当它们积累起来时，会在一定程度上抑制你的同理心。

sentences.en: So I had to find a way to build it up again because I'm beginning to really like being more empathic.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须找到一种方法来重新建立它，因为我开始真的很喜欢变得更有同理心。

sentences.en: So I thought it has to do with relating to other people.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这与如何与他人建立联系有关。

sentences.en: So suppose I go through the day and people I run into like a cashier at a diner or people that I'm friendly with.
sentences.zh: 假设我过了一天，遇到了一些人，比如餐馆的收银员，或者我熟悉的人。

sentences.en: And if I spend more than a few seconds with them while we're talking, I try to figure out what they're feeling or what they're going through.
sentences.zh: 如果我们在交谈时相处超过几秒钟，我会试着去弄清楚他们的感受或正在经历的事情。

sentences.en: What what's their perspective?
sentences.zh: 他们的视角是什么？

sentences.en: Where do they stand inside their head?
sentences.zh: 他们在想些什么？

sentences.en: And I would find I'd get a little more opened up to them.
sentences.zh: 我会发现自己对他们更加敞开心扉了。

sentences.en: And and that's what happened by the time I talked to that cab driver.
sentences.zh: 而这就是我与那位出租车司机交谈时发生的情况。

sentences.en: I've been practicing this so much that I actually wasn't wasn't angry with them anymore.
sentences.zh: 我练习得太多了，以至于我真的不再对他们生气了。

sentences.en: And I noticed that it it seems to happen even if I don't name the emotion.
sentences.zh: 而且我注意到，即使我不去命名那种情绪，这种情况似乎也会发生。

sentences.en: I thought it would be important to name the emotion.
sentences.zh: 我原以为命名情绪很重要。

sentences.en: And I guess that does because you can't always name the emotion.
sentences.zh: 我想确实如此，因为你并不总能准确说出那种情绪。

sentences.en: You don't really know for sure.
sentences.zh: 你并不真的确定。

sentences.en: But maybe making the effort to name it puts you in touch with them better.
sentences.zh: 但也许努力去命名它能让你更好地与他们产生共鸣。

sentences.en: But I also notice if I'm just noticing the color of their eyes and taking it in, you have very nice brown eyes.
sentences.zh: 但我也注意到，如果我只是观察他们的眼睛颜色并用心感受，比如你有一双非常好看的棕色眼睛。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I didn't notice that till now.
sentences.zh: 我直到现在才注意到。

sentences.en: And, you know, it took me about a half an hour before I knew you had a beard, which is proof to me that we all can improve on letting each other in.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我花了大约半小时才发现你有胡子，这对我来说证明了我们都可以改善彼此之间的接纳度。

sentences.en: And because you can talk to some I know in my experience, I'll be talking to somebody for 10 minutes and I'll say, are you really looking at this person?
sentences.zh: 因为你可以和某人交谈，我知道根据我的经验，我会和某人交谈10分钟，然后我会问自己，你真的在看着这个人吗？

sentences.en: And I realized there's a blob where the face ought to be.
sentences.zh: 我意识到本该是脸的地方却是一片模糊。

sentences.en: And that doesn't help connect with the other person, because I think when I really see you, I think something changes on my face.
sentences.zh: 这无助于与对方建立联系，因为我认为当我真正看到你时，我的脸上会有所变化。

sentences.en: I think I get a little more focused on you and a little more related.
sentences.zh: 我想我会更专注于你，与你建立更多联系。

sentences.en: And then I see something change on your face.
sentences.zh: 然后我看到你的脸上也有所变化。

sentences.en: I think it's a dynamic interaction where you're changed by how I'm changed.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种动态的互动，你因我的改变而改变。

sentences.en: And it goes on and on like that.
sentences.zh: 就这样循环往复。

sentences.en: And we have a much better chance of getting together on what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我们也就更有可能在谈话内容上达成共识。

sentences.en: And by our connecting, the people watching us have a greater incentive, a greater impulse to pay attention to us.
sentences.zh: 通过我们的连接，观看我们的人会有更大的动力、更大的冲动去关注我们。

sentences.en: Because when two people are relating, it's hard not to look at them.
sentences.zh: 因为当两个人正在建立联系时，很难不去看他们。

sentences.en: Alan Alda's book is called, If I Understood You, Would I Have This Look On My Face?
sentences.zh: 艾伦·阿尔达的书名为《如果我理解了你，我的脸上会有这种表情吗？》

sentences.en: My Adventures in the Art and Science of Relating and Communicating.
sentences.zh: 《我在人际关系与沟通艺术与科学中的冒险》。

sentences.zh: 我们今天的对话是在华盛顿特区埃德洛维奇犹太社区中心的现场观众面前录制的。

sentences.en: Alan Alda, thanks for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 艾伦·阿尔达，感谢你今天参加《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.zh: 本期节目由玛吉·彭曼和塔拉·博伊尔制作，她们本身就是出色的沟通者。

sentences.zh: 我们的员工包括普拉特·沙阿、雷娜·科恩、珍妮·施密特和蕾妮·克拉尔。

sentences.zh: 我们本周的幕后英雄是雪莉·苏拉茨基、艾米丽·吉尔森和JCC的埃利奥特·莱恩斯。

sentences.zh: 雪莉、埃利奥特和艾米丽帮助我们录制了与艾伦·阿尔达的对话。

sentences.en: At one point, while we were playing video clips from Alan's acting career, we had some technical difficulties with the projector.
sentences.zh: 在某一时刻，当我们播放艾伦演艺生涯的视频片段时，投影仪出现了一些技术故障。

sentences.en: It wouldn't turn off after playing the clips.
sentences.zh: 播放完片段后它无法关闭。

sentences.en: So Shirley held a cardboard UPS mailer in front of that projector for the next 60 minutes
sentences.zh: 所以雪莉在接下来的60分钟里，一直拿着一个纸板UPS快递袋挡在投影仪前，

sentences.en: to ensure the audience wasn't distracted by a square box of light over the stage.
sentences.zh: 以确保观众不会被舞台上方那块方形的光斑所干扰。

sentences.en: If that isn't the selfless act of an unsung hero, I don't know what is.
sentences.zh: 如果这还算不上幕后英雄的无私行为，我不知道什么才算了。
